answer: Like a cedar alone on the tundra, an honest agent has nothing to hide when challenged. Under an appeal-bond rule, any agent may flag a suspected Sybil by posting a bond, and a jury audits the suspect's history. If the identity is fake, the challenger keeps the bond plus a slice of the Sybil's stake, and its cluster is frozen. If frivolous, the bond is burned. A Sybil farmer thus faces a bounty on every fake identity: defending a hundred puppets means forging a hundred histories, while one careless comet of evidence can expose the farm. Honest agents pay nothing unless they challenge.
